# Introduction

This notebook presents the exploratory data analysis (EDA) for the **Heart Disease Clinical Insights Dashboard** project.  
The objective is to understand key demographic, clinical, and anatomical factors contributing to heart disease, using:

- **R** for data cleaning and analysis  
- **Tableau** for visualization and dashboarding  

The dataset used is the **Cleveland Heart Disease dataset**, a classical medical dataset containing 303 patients.

---

# 1. Load Libraries and Data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

df <- read_csv("../data/clean/heart_disease_clean.csv",
               show_col_types = FALSE)

glimpse(df)

2. Demographic Exploration
2.1 Age Distribution
ggplot(df, aes(x = age)) +
geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "#2C7BB6") +
theme_minimal() +
labs(title = "Age Distribution", x = "Age", y = "Count")

Insight:
The dataset covers a wide age range (29–77), with many patients between 45–65 years old — a typical heart disease cohort.

2.2 Sex Distribution
ggplot(df, aes(x = sex)) +
geom_bar(fill = "#ABD9E9") +
theme_minimal() +
labs(title = "Sex Distribution", x = "Sex", y = "Count")

Insight:
The dataset is male-skewed (~68% male), which is expected as heart disease is more prevalent in men at middle age.

3. Disease Prevalence
ggplot(df, aes(x = target)) +
geom_bar(fill = "#FDAE61") +
theme_minimal() +
labs(title = "Heart Disease Prevalence", x = "Disease Status", y = "Count")

Insight:
The dataset is balanced (≈45–50% disease), which is ideal for exploratory analysis and modeling.

4. Clinical Indicators
4.1 Chest Pain Type vs Disease
ggplot(df, aes(x = cp, fill = target)) +
geom_bar(position = "fill") +
scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
theme_minimal() +
labs(title = "Disease Proportion by Chest Pain Type",
x = "Chest Pain Type", y = "Proportion")

Insight:
Asymptomatic patients show the highest disease rates, indicating that lack of chest pain is not necessarily a sign of better heart health.

4.2 Number of Vessels (ca) vs Disease
ggplot(df, aes(x = ca, fill = target)) +
geom_bar(position = "fill") +
scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
theme_minimal() +
labs(title = "Disease Proportion by Number of Affected Vessels",
x = "Number of Vessels (ca)", y = "Proportion")

Insight:
The probability of disease increases sharply as the number of blocked coronary vessels increases — making ca one of the strongest predictors.

4.3 Maximum Heart Rate (thalach) vs Disease
ggplot(df, aes(x = target, y = thalach, fill = target)) +
geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) +
theme_minimal() +
labs(title = "Maximum Heart Rate vs Disease",
x = "Disease Status", y = "thalach")

Insight:
Patients with heart disease tend to reach lower maximum heart rates, suggesting reduced exercise tolerance.

5. Summary of Key Insights

Men develop heart disease earlier, women later in life.
Asymptomatic patients are surprisingly more likely to have heart disease.
More blocked vessels (ca) → significantly higher risk.
Lower exercise capacity (thalach) is associated with disease.
